name: Vegetarian Beyaynetu

ingredients.name: collard greens or sturdy spinach, chopped

steps: Soak the rinsed yellow split peas in some of the measured water for 60 minutes, then drain and reserve the soaking water. Rinse the red lentils separately. Dice the onion and divide it into 100 g for the red lentils, 50 g for the peas, 40 g for cabbage and 30 g for greens. Use oil rather than spiced butter to keep all four portions plant-based.

For misir wot, heat 20 ml oil in a saucepan and soften the 100 g onion for 6 minutes. Add 7 g garlic, 7 g ginger and the berbere; stir for 1 minute. Add red lentils, 450 ml water and 4 g salt. Simmer uncovered for 20–25 minutes, stirring and adding a splash of the reserved water if needed, until thick and tender.

For kik alicha, heat 15 ml oil in another pan and soften 50 g onion for 5 minutes. Add 4 g garlic, 4 g ginger and 2 g turmeric for 30 seconds. Add drained split peas, 550 ml water and 3 g salt. Simmer covered for 35–45 minutes until soft but not watery; stir near the end so the peas do not stick.

For tikil gomen, heat 15 ml oil and cook 40 g onion for 3 minutes. Add the remaining 4 g ginger, 3 g turmeric, diced carrot and potato, 120 ml water and 3 g salt. Cover and cook 10 minutes. Add cabbage and cook uncovered another 10–12 minutes until all vegetables are tender and the liquid has mostly evaporated.

For gomen, heat the remaining 10 ml oil with the remaining 30 g onion and 4 g garlic for 3 minutes. Add chopped greens, the remaining 180 ml water and 2 g salt. Cover for 5 minutes, then uncover and cook until the greens are tender and no liquid pools in the pan. Toss diced tomato with lemon juice just before serving.

Lay a large piece of injera across a platter and keep extra injera rolled at the side. Spoon the red lentils, yellow peas, cabbage-carrot-potato mix and greens into four separate mounds on the bread, with the fresh tomato salad in a small fifth area. Serve immediately for four people, tearing pieces of injera to pick up each component.
tips: Beyaynetu is a platter of separate dishes, not a single mixed stew. The reviewed photo shows red lentils, yellow split peas, dark greens, turmeric cabbage with carrot and potato, and tomato salad arranged in distinct mounds over spongy injera.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
